summary.oneLiner: EPL delivered record Q4 revenue growth of 17.6% driven by a structural shift to high-margin Beauty & Cosmetics (30% growth), while announcing a transformational merger with Indovida to create a $1B platform. Management navigates Middle East raw material volatility with >50% contractual pass-through coverage, ensuring margin protection despite near-term cost inflation.

one-line thesis: EPL delivered record Q4 revenue growth of 17.6% driven by a structural shift to high-margin Beauty & Cosmetics (30% growth), while announcing a transformational merger with Indovida to create a $1B platform. Management navigates Middle East raw material volatility with >50% contractual pass-through coverage, ensuring margin protection despite near-term cost inflation.
financial scorecard: Revenue +17.6% YoY (Q4), +13% YoY (FY26); EBITDA +17.2% YoY (Q4) at 20.2% margin, FY26 margin 20.4%; PAT (normalized) +1% YoY (Q4), +15% YoY (FY26); Order Book: Strong pipeline in Thailand/Brazil; Net Debt/EBITDA improved to 0.52x. One-offs: Q4 PAT impacted by CEO transition costs and phasing reversal in AMESA; Merger expenses largely booked in Q4.
guidance: Revenue growth 11-13% (long-term structural guide); Margins sustained >20% with full cost pass-through expected; Order inflow robust in B&C; Capex elevated (~INR 480cr FY26) to support B&C/Thailand, will moderate post-commissioning.
order book & pipeline: Pipeline strong in Thailand (validation ongoing) and Brazil (multi-customer expansion); China core market performing strongly; No specific monetary value disclosed but conversion rates high.
segment / subsidiary detail: Beauty & Cosmetics: +30% YoY (Q4), now >40% of mix; Oral Care: +10% YoY (Q4), recovering from headwinds; Regional: EAP +25%, Americas +24.1%, Europe +15.5%, AMESA +10.4%, India +11.5%.
growth verticals / optionality: Thailand greenfield plant (commissioned Nov '25) ramping up in FY27; Indovida merger adds scale/emerging market footprint; Active M&A hunt for geography/capability add-ons in B&C space.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin 20.2% (Q4); >50% business under contractual landed-cost-plus-power pass-through; Non-contractual pricing proactive with no expected lag; Middle East crisis impacting RM availability/costs but fully recoverable.
capex / expansion: FY26 Capex INR 480cr+ (vs Depreciation INR 385cr); Driven by B&C capacity, innovation, and Thailand plant ($5mn portion); FY27 capex expected to remain elevated before normalizing.
capital allocation: Dividend suspended until merger completion (est. Q4 FY27) to preserve valuation construct; Net debt/EBITDA at 0.52x allows flexibility; Cash prioritized for organic capex and inorganic M&A; Debt paydown secondary to growth funding.
risks & watch-items: Middle East geopolitical crisis extending RM shortage/cost volatility; Merger regulatory approval delays (SEBI/CCI/Global antitrust); Thailand plant ramp-up slower than expected; Currency translation impacts on EBIT.
management quality / tone: Confident and agile; Emphasizes 'muscle' built post-COVID for pricing; Transparent on merger constraints (no data sharing yet); Optimistic on B&C structural growth despite macro headwinds.
non-obvious takeaways: Thailand plant contributed negligible volume in Q4 despite 25% EAP growth (driven by China); Dividend halt is regulatory/structural due to swap mechanics, not cash crunch; EBIT margin expanded 50bps FYoY despite heavy depreciation from new capex.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material inflation and supply scarcity due to Middle East crisis | Uflex Limited | beneficiary | Med | As a peer in flexible packaging with similar pass-through mechanisms, sector-wide pricing power validation benefits Uflex if EPL successfully maintains margins. |
| Consolidation of packaging supply base reducing vendor options | Small-cap unlisted tube converters | loser | High | EPL-Indovida merger creates a $1B entity with superior scale/ESG ratings, potentially squeezing smaller players out of premium MNC contracts. |

scorecard.pe_basis: TTM trailing (spec band written for forward P/E)

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.
